Definition: from G4862 and G5346; to say jointly, i.e. assent to:--consent unto.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says that if he does what he would not, he consents to the law that it is good. Even while he fails to do it, his conscience agrees with God's law, and that agreement is the proof that the law is good and he is the one at fault.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that agreeing with God's law even when I break it is the beginning of honesty, and I believe a conscience that still says the law is good has not yet gone hard.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
